start_here: Connect your URT-2 board to start
start_here_det: Plug the URT-2 into this computer with its USB cable, then press “Connect URT-2”.
unsupported: This browser cannot talk to USB devices. Open this page in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge on a Windows, Mac, Linux or ChromeOS computer.
unsupported_short: Please use Chrome or Edge on a computer
connect_hint: Chrome lists the USB servo boards it finds. Pick the URT-2: “USB Single Serial” on a Mac, “USB Serial Device (COM…)” on Windows.
show_all_ports: My adapter is not in the list
ready: Connected. Choose the IDs and press “Start numbering”.
ready_det: You can number servos with only USB power. Centering needs the servo power supply.
force_1m: Also set every servo to 1 Mbps (recommended)
one_at_a_time: Plug in ONE servo at a time. All new servos come as ID 1, so two of them on the bus would answer together.
plug_next: Plug in one servo — it becomes ID {n}
plug_next_det: Any baud rate is found automatically.
remove_first: Unplug servo {id} first, then plug in the next one
already: This servo already got ID {id}. Plug in the next one.
done: ID {n} done — unplug it and label it
new_model: new model: power it off and on, then check the chain once
finished_det: Chain the servos together and press “Check the chain”.
bad_range: Start ID must be between 0 and the last ID (max 253)
io_lost: Lost the connection to the URT-2
io_lost_det: Plug it back in and press “Connect URT-2”.
collision: More than one servo seems to be connected
collision_det: Keep only one servo plugged in.
error_det: Check the cable; it will retry.
check_hint: Connect all numbered servos in a chain and scan IDs 0–253 at 1 Mbps.
none_found: No servo answered at 1 Mbps. Check the cable, or number the servos first.
duplicates: Two or more servos share ID {ids}. Unplug them and number them again one at a time.
center_hint: Before you fit a horn or an arm, turn the servo to its middle (2048). Connect one servo and its power supply. The shaft will turn.
center_none: No single servo found. Connect exactly one servo.
centered: Servo {id} is centered and holding. Fit the horn, then press “Release”.
center_power_det: Connect the servo power supply (7.4 V or 12 V, as your servo needs).
duck_note: Microduck joint IDs, as used by the HD-1910 replica builds. The servos are numbered in this order. The preset also ticks the protection box: over-current and over-voltage protection are off from the factory. When all are done, power the servos off and on, then press “Check the chain” to read the IDs and the protection back.
protect: Switch on over-current and over-voltage protection (off from the factory; recommended for HD-1910)
protect_skipped: protection not changed: not available on this model
